title: Forgeon
method: producthunt api v2 (top launches, last 2d) + startup-worthiness score

zh.gap: 它对着的是互动小说爱好者，一个不大且早就被服务过的人群——AI Dungeon 和角色聊天类产品几年前就到了。没有人把同一套机器指向那个只想要一件成品的人：一本有自家孩子名字、有自家孩子画的、能印出来的故事。
zh.pain: 家长不想要一个类型，也不想要一个社区。他要一个故事，就今晚，主角是孩子喜欢的人，而且有结尾——还得在孩子困到听不进去之前拿到。
zh.kill: 互动小说四十年来一直是个小而热忱的市场，AI 没有把它做大，只是把供给做成了无限——这恰恰是平台最不需要的东西。愿意付钱的那批人被 Character.ai 一类占着，而平台经济学要的创作者飞轮它拿不到。而对这个切口本身，危险是另一种且更尖锐：睡前是家长刻意留出的无屏时刻，任何一眼看出「是机器写的」的东西，在唯一重要的那个评审面前当场失效。
zh.move: 扔掉平台和市集，只出一件成品。一本短的、有插图的、可分支的故事，用孩子自己的名字和他自己的画，十分钟做完，能导成 PDF 或印成书——那才是家长真会付钱并且留下来的东西。形态上优先「念给他听」，不是「显示给他看」。冷启动（中文）：小红书「睡前故事 编不出来」「绘本 定制」的评论区，以及亲子共读号下面排队的那批人；（英文）：r/Parenting、r/daddit 里讲睡前故事讲干了的帖子，以及定制绘本相关版块里互相报价的人。
zh.hook: 晚上八点四十的家长，这一周同样三个故事已经讲完了，没词了——而孩子要求自己在故事里。这件事附近的付费行为本来就不小：定制儿童绘本是实打实要花钱的，印出来、寄到家。
zh.does: 生成式互动小说。真正值得做的版本是把同一套机器指向一件成品：今晚的睡前故事，里面有这个孩子，十分钟讲完。
zh.consumer_angle: 家长拿走的是一本有自家孩子在里面、能打印的成品书——正是终端用户闸门明确留的那个例外：AI 直接产出人能拿在手上的成品。

gap: It is aimed at the interactive-fiction hobbyist, a small and long-served audience — AI Dungeon and the character-chat apps got there years ago. Nobody has pointed the same machinery at the person who wants one finished, illustrated, printable story with their own child's name and their own child's drawings in it.
pain: The parent does not want a genre or a community. They want one story, tonight, starring someone their child loves, that ends — and they want it before the child is too tired to hear it.
kill: Interactive fiction has been a small, passionate market for forty years and AI has not enlarged it — it has made supply infinite, which is the opposite of what a marketplace needs. Character.ai and its clones own the audience that would pay, and platform economics need a creator flywheel this will not get. For the wedge itself the danger is different and sharper: a bedtime story is a moment parents deliberately keep screen-free, and anything that reads as 'the machine wrote it' fails in front of the only critic who matters.
move: Drop the platform and the marketplace; ship one artefact. A short illustrated branching story with the child's own name and their own drawings in it, done in ten minutes, exportable as a PDF or a printed book — the thing a parent would actually pay for and keep. Read it aloud rather than displaying it. Cold start (Chinese): 小红书 「睡前故事 编不出来」「绘本 定制」 comment sections, and the queues under 亲子共读 accounts; (English): r/Parenting and r/daddit threads about running out of bedtime stories, and the personalised-book subreddits where people compare what they paid.
hook: A parent at 20:40 who has told the same three stories all week and is out of material — and whose child wants to be in the story. The nearby paying behaviour is already large: personalised children's books sell for real money, printed and shipped.
does: Generative interactive fiction. The version worth building points the same machinery at one artefact instead: tonight's bedtime story, with this child in it, finished in ten minutes.
consumer_angle: A parent walks away with a finished, printable book their child is in — the one exception the end-user gate explicitly allows: AI producing a deliverable a person can hold.
